chunks: Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtha al-Bahili narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to us in the year 273 AH, saying: Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari narrated to us in the year 229 AH, from Abu al-Jarood, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said to me: O Abu al-Jarood,

When the orbit turns and people say: He has died or perished, and followed an unknown valley, and the seekers say to him: How can it be that he returns when his bones have been perished? Then at that time, expect him. And when you hear of his appearance, join him even if crawling on the ice.

key_terms.الْفَلَك: The orbit/sphere (metaphor for time or the world)
key_terms.دَارَ الْفَلَكُ: The orbit turns (referring to the passage of time or the cycle of events)

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of doubt during the occultation of the Mahdi and how should believers respond?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the psychological trials of the Major Occultation, where skeptics use the physical decay of the body ('bones') to deny the Imam's continued existence. Imam al-Baqir (AS) advises believers to remain expectant (*irtajoo*) and to seek him out eagerly, even if crawling through snow, emphasizing that spiritual vigilance outweighs physical hardship or logical doubt.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (12) Abu Sulayman Ahmad bin Hawtha al-Bahili narrated from Ibraheem bin Iss’haq an-Nahawandi from Abdullah bin Hammad al-Ansari from Abul-Jarood that Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) had said to him: “O Abul-Jarood,

if the orbit turns and people say that he (al-Mahdi) has died, perished or followed an unknown valley and the opponents say that how he will be back whereas his bones have been perished, then you are to expect him and if you hear of his appearance, you are to join him even if crawling on the ice.”
